name: RESI — Institute for Responsible Superintelligence
new_details: RESI (Institute for Responsible Superintelligence) is a nonprofit research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts building the scientific foundations for superintelligence that is "safe by design," applying the cryptography playbook of precise definitions, constructions, composition, and impossibility results to AI safety. It was founded by Turing Award winner Shafi Goldwasser, cryptographer Vinod Vaikuntanathan, and former OpenAI Safety Systems researcher Adam Tauman Kalai, with a research team spanning computer science, mathematics, economics, law, and ethics. Work is organized into AI-assisted working groups (verification and delegation, modular architectures, incentives, cryptographic and legal mechanisms), with an active visitor program; topics and working group leaders are still to be announced.

name: Verified Mechanisms
new_details: Verified Mechanisms is an independent, grant-funded research project (funded via Manifund) building a formally verified autoresearch pipeline for theoretical mechanistic interpretability, where multiple frontier LLM agents collaborate to generate theorems that are machine-checked in Lean 4. The pilot problem asks how many attention heads are needed to compute a Boolean function, and outputs include an open-source multi-agent orchestration harness and the xorformer theorem ledger repository. The team states it plans to onboard additional researchers over the coming months for multi-agent orchestration and mech interp work — there is no formal application form, but interested people can join the Discord or email hello@verifiedmechanisms.ai.
